View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/3bd8a492-ff61-41db-a7f2-c821d481fd72/BD_NL_QuoteCircle.png?t=1781794162)
Caption: 

“The more precisely the position is determined, the less precisely the momentum is known.”
_— Werner Heisenberg_



----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d85e5e50-1d2c-4f7f-8262-ffca2d4ae74d/unnamed.jpg?t=1793137220)
Caption: 

# The Heisenberg principle of investing

According to the rules of quantum mechanics, matter is wavy: Every discrete particle also exists as a wave of probability.

This makes them difficult to pin down. To know a particle’s position, you have to collapse its waviness into a single point, which leaves it with no definite wavelength. To know its momentum, you have to let the wave ripple across space, which leaves the particle with no fixed position.

Hence the Heisenberg uncertainty principle: The more you know about the position of a particle, the less you know about its momentum.

Something similar happens in markets.

The fundamental principle of _investing_ is that the intrinsic value of any asset is equal to the net present value of all its future cash flows.

Logically, then, the most accurate way to value a company’s stock is to estimate all its future cash flows.

But this is difficult. Who knows what a company’s earnings will be in a decade or two? Or whether it will exist even. Usually, the best we can hope to do is forecast earnings just a year or two out.

So that’s how we trade them, as well. Stocks are typically valued as a multiple of next year’s earnings because that’s the easiest metric to calculate with a reasonable amount of precision.

But precision comes at the expense of usefulness: A one-year forecast captures only a tiny sliver of a company’s intrinsic value.

It’s a tradeoff investors have to make — the more precisely a metric can be measured, the less useful it is for determining value.

# THE BIG ONE

## 🏦 Ripple gains final OCC approval for national trust bank


----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/97b056d2-3dc0-416d-bb7b-9a4bbcc1ae59/ripple-occ-1200x675.png?t=1793131896) [Ripple]
Follow image link: (https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-10-26-ripple-gains-final-occ-approval-rlusd-431810)
Caption: 

----------
Ripple has received final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to launch a national trust bank. The bank will oversee reserves backing Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin and offer digital asset custody services to businesses.

* Ripple National Trust Bank can manage RLUSD's segregated reserves, serve as collateral trustee for stablecoin holders and provide fiduciary digital asset custody services.

* RLUSD will still be issued by Standard Custody & Trust Company, Ripple's New York-regulated trust company. Ripple applied for the OCC charter in July
